title: Mass Euroscepticism revisited: The role of distributive justice

selected_claim.evidence_location: Table 1, Model 3, and Figure 1(a), Results section
selected_claim.evidence_summary: In the multilevel model, the association between perceived earnings injustice and Euroscepticism varies with country corruption levels. Figure 1(a) shows a positive association in countries with low corruption (higher CPI scores), while the association is not significant at high corruption levels. This is an adjusted observational association, not evidence from random assignment.
selected_claim.x: Perceived earnings injustice: respondents' assessment of whether their net pay or income from a pension or social benefits is unfairly low, coded so higher values indicate greater perceived under-rewarding.
selected_claim.y: Euroscepticism: respondents' position on an 11-point scale about whether European unification has gone too far or should go further, coded so higher values indicate stronger Eurosceptic attitudes.
selected_claim.target_population: Respondents in the 23 EU member states participating in the 2018 European Social Survey, specifically respondents in countries with low corruption levels (higher Corruption Perceptions Index scores).
selected_claim.adjustment_description: Table 1, Model 3 adjusts for the other individual-level distributive-injustice measures, individual socio-demographic and attitudinal controls, and country-level controls. It includes country corruption and its interaction with earnings injustice; Figure 1(a) presents the conditional association across corruption levels.
covariates: Relative household income category, including a missing-income category
Social spending as a percentage of GDP

article_review.evidence: In the multilevel model, the association between perceived earnings injustice and Euroscepticism varies with country corruption levels. Figure 1(a) shows a positive association in countries with low corruption (higher CPI scores), while the association is not significant at high corruption levels. This is an adjusted observational association, not evidence from random assignment.
article_review.evidence_location: Table 1, Model 3, and Figure 1(a), Results section
article_review.adjustment: Table 1, Model 3 adjusts for the other individual-level distributive-injustice measures, individual socio-demographic and attitudinal controls, and country-level controls. It includes country corruption and its interaction with earnings injustice; Figure 1(a) presents the conditional association across corruption levels.

evidence_summary: The focal paper estimates the association between perceived earnings injustice (greater perceived under-rewarding) and Eurosceptic sentiment, with the claim focused on respondents in low-corruption EU member states. Model 3 adjusts for other individual-level distributive-injustice measures, socio-demographic and attitudinal controls, and country-level controls, including corruption and its interaction with earnings injustice. Figure 1(a) presents the conditional association across corruption levels. The supplied claim describes an observational conditional association; no additional causal-identification result is supplied here.
x_definition: Perceived unfairness of one's own earnings or remuneration: respondent judgments that personal net pay, pension income, or social benefits are unjustly low or inadequate relative to deserved reward.
y_definition: Euroscepticism: negative attitudes toward the European Union and opposition to European integration, including sentiment that integration has gone too far and preferences to constrain or reverse integration.

splits.description: Negative orientations toward the European Union and opposition to European integration, including Euroscepticism and preferences to limit or reverse integration.

Perceived distributive fairness of personal remuneration or economic rewards, including fairness of pay, earnings, income, pensions or benefits relative to deservingness, contribution, or entitlement.
